messages:
Nisha: Quick proposal — instead of full replays on midflight retries, have the edge "borrow" the backend stream ownership and issue a compact control-frame that allows a resumed connection to pick up from the same token/kv checkpoint. want feedback on safety/perf tradeoffs.
Oliver: Sounds interesting. main questions: how do we guarantee cache/KV validity across handoff? and what about partial-token duplication?
Nisha: Good Q. Idea is: when borrowing, edge keeps a short immutable resume_token that encodes model-id, model-commit, kv-checksum, and last-output-index. backend must be able to validate resume_token and accept a resume handshake that includes idempotency key. If checksum mismatches -> reject and fall back.
Samir: Concern: head-of-line and backpressure. If we allow edge to hold ownership, could it block resources on backend while waiting for client reconnect? we need a lease TTL and decay policy.
Sylvia: Agree on TTL. Proposal: borrow lease with two phases: 1) short hard lease (e.g. 2s) for immediate resume; 2) soft grace (e.g. 30s) where backend keeps compacted state but can drop if pressured. Edge will advertise intent-to-resume flag to trigger tiered retention.
Nisha: Exactly. Also propose a lightweight control-frame protocol so we don't need full HTTP re-establish. Example control frame JSON: 
```json
{
  "control": "resume_request",
  "resume_token": "r_abc123",
  "idempotency_key": "cli-7890",
  "last_seq": 4321
}
```
Oliver: Nice. How do we prevent duplication if client already received some final bytes and then resumes? last_seq should help but need server-side dedupe of repeated emission. That adds bookkeeping per-lease. Cost vs benefit?
Samir: From infra POV: cost is small if we compact by seq-window. Keep only recent N seq entries for dedupe and set TTL. For long-running streams we can require explicit checkpointing from client at logical boundaries.
Sylvia: Also need to define failure modes: if resume rejected -> edge should either (a) fall back to hedging to secondary model variant, or (b) attempt a strict replay with warnings to caller. We should expose policy config per-route.
deploy-bot: Prototype push: staging edge implements resume_request handler behind feature flag. Canary 10% of streaming routes.
QA-Bot: Test note: resume acceptance currently fails for quantized-variant models due to mismatch in kv-checksum. Filing test-case: "resume/quantize-checksum".
Nisha: Thanks. Action items: (1) write protocol doc with control-frame fields + error codes, (2) define lease TTL defaults and pressure eviction signals, (3) add per-route policy config for fallback behavior. I'll draft RFC followup.
Oliver: +1 on RFC. Also add metric for resume_success_rate and resume_fallback_count.
Samir: Add quota implication note — borrowed leases count towards backend concurrency until grace expires.
Sylvia: I'll sketch API surface for route-level flags (resume_enabled, fallback: [hedge|replay|reject], lease_ttl).
Nisha: Perfect. If nobody objects, I'll open the RFC follow-up PR tomorrow. :+1:
